styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Viking ships, the Opera and the Royal Palace.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Fjord ferries, forest trails and Holmenkollen views.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Munch, Vigeland's sculptures and the Astrup Fearnley.

stays.why: Walk to the Opera, Karl Johans gate and the palace; best transport links for day trips.
Waterfront dining and the ferry pier to Bygdøy museums and the islands.
Cafés, bars and a local feel along the Akerselva river; trams to the centre.
Quiet and central-west; close to Vigeland Park and the T-bane to Holmenkollen.

food: Try Norwegian basics: salmon, fish soup, kjøttkaker (meat cakes) and brown cheese on bread.
Lunch is the cheaper meal. Many restaurants serve the same dishes at lower midday prices.
Mathallen food hall at Vulkan has many small vendors; good for picky eaters and rainy days.
Seafood counters and the fish market area near the harbour are worth a look; check prices first, Norway is costly.
Tap water is safe and free. Alcohol is sold in state Vinmonopolet shops; bars are expensive.
more_time: Take a fjord ferry to the islands for a half-day of walking and swimming in summer.
Swap one museum for a forest walk or a trip up to Holmenkollen for views over the city.
Add a day trip by train to a nearby town; check timetables and prices on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the museums, the Opera and a fjord or forest outing; add a night for Bygdøy and Holmenkollen.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near -1°C and lows around -6°C. Pack warm layers and expect icy pavements.
February: still cold, highs near 1°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
March: slowly warmer, highs near 5°C, but nights still below freezing.
April: highs near 10°C, lows near 1°C. Mild days, but keep a jacket.
May: highs near 16°C and long bright evenings. A great month to walk the city.
June: mild and bright, highs near 21°C. Pack a light rain layer; about 12 rain days.
July: warmest month, highs near 21°C. Busy; book hotels early.
August: still warm, highs near 20°C. About 13 rain days, so bring an umbrella.
September: cooler, highs near 16°C. Good for museums and forest walks.
October: highs near 10°C, lows near 5°C. Wet and grey; dress for rain.
November: cold and dark, highs near 4°C. Fewer crowds, shorter days.
December: cold, highs near 1°C, lows near -4°C. Dark days; check for snow and ice.

climate_guide.summary: Cool coastal climate: mild summers, cold winters and rain in every month. Days are very long in summer and short in winter.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 16–21°C and long daylight. Best for fjord ferries, parks and walking.

items.title: Winters are cold
items.text: January and February highs sit near -1 to 1°C with lows of -6 to -5°C. Bring a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 8–13 rain days every month. A waterproof jacket beats an umbrella in wind.

items.title: Big daylight swing
items.text: Summer evenings stay bright late; December days are short. Plan outdoor sights for midday in winter.

items.title: Watch for ice
items.text: Winter pavements can be slippery. Wear shoes with grip or bring traction aids.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket and comfortable walking shoes. Add a warm hat and gloves from November to March.

transit.best: Walk in the centre and use the Ruter app for metro, trams and buses.

modes.text: The T-bane covers the city and suburbs. Buy tickets in the Ruter app or at kiosks.
Buses fill the gaps; same Ruter tickets work across metro, tram and bus.
Uber and Bolt operate. Taxis are expensive; Oslo Taxi and NorgesTaxi are reliable.
Not recommended: tolls and limited parking. Use transit instead.
The centre is compact and easy on foot; bike-sharing is available.
Ferries connect to the Bygdøy museums and the fjord islands.
